facts.value: Datalink Corporation (Minnesota; IT services and solutions for midsize and large companies)
Insight Enterprises, Inc. (Delaware), through its wholly owned subsidiary Reef Acquisition Co.
Strategic: Fortune 500-ranked global provider of IT hardware, software, cloud and service solutions (p. 1)
$11.25 per share in cash, without interest (p. 2). Funded from Insight cash and existing credit facilities; no financing condition (p. 48).
Bidder-led: Party A's unsolicited January 2016 proposal started the process; the target then ran a broad auction from June 2016.
Met (process 1): 23 parties (10 strategic incl. Party A, Party B and Insight; 13 financial incl. Party C)

facts.field: Currency and units of bid prices

facts.value: Datalink's sale began with Party A's unsolicited $10.00 cash proposal in January 2016. The board hired Raymond James and gave Party A an NDA; in April it declined Party A's financing-contingent $10.30-$10.75 proposal. From June 2016 Raymond James approached 27 buyers, 23 of which signed NDAs; nine sent initial indications and the board also counted Party A's standing proposal. The board advanced the five highest bidders and asked for final proposals with merger-agreement mark-ups by 08/30: Party B bid $12.00, Party C $11.00 then $11.25, Insight $11.75 then $12.00, and two did not bid. Insight got exclusivity on 09/02, but its pre-closing 8-K demands led the board to let exclusivity lapse and re-approach Parties B and C; Party B withdrew after seeing third-quarter results, and Party C, at $11.25, was denied the new financials. Insight regained exclusivity on 10/26 and cut its price to $11.00 on 11/01, then agreed to $11.25 on 11/02; the merger agreement was signed on 11/06/2016 and announced on 11/07/2016.

findings.title: Austin's ruling: January bilateral stage is round 1
findings.detail: A 21 September audit of an earlier Datalink draft asked whether E6's ordering puts round 1 at the June 6 outreach, leaving Party A's pre-June activity in a round 0. Austin ruled to retain January's bilateral stage as round 1 and June's broad outreach as round 2, with five rounds overall. January 29 remains an inferred opening date. The adjudication calls this a case-level mapping decision, not an instruction change.

recorded_decision.decision: Retain January's bilateral stage as round 1 and June's broad outreach as round 2; keep five rounds. January 29 remains inferred.
